---
title: Mizani
---

Mizani provides tools for building scales in Python graphics systems. It
is based on the R [scales](https://scales.r-lib.org) package, and
[plotnine](https://plotnine.org) uses it for all its scales.

A scale maps data values to values suitable for visual properties, such
as coordinates, sizes or colour codes. The graphics system draws the plot
from these mapped values. A scale also chooses which values to mark on a
guide and how to label them.
Mizani provides functions and classes for these tasks, which a graphics
system can combine to build its scales.

## Example

Take five values that span nearly five orders of magnitude.

```{python}
import numpy as np

x = np.array([12, 150, 1_800, 23_000, 410_000])
```

[](`~mizani.bounds.rescale`) maps the values to $[0, 1]$, and a palette
maps the rescaled values to colours.
[](`~mizani.breaks.breaks_extended`) chooses the values to mark on the
guide, and [](`~mizani.labels.label_comma`) formats their labels.

```{python}
from mizani.bounds import rescale
from mizani.breaks import breaks_extended
from mizani.labels import label_comma
from mizani.palettes import gradient_n_pal

palette = gradient_n_pal(["#132B43", "#56B1F7"])
limits = (x.min(), x.max())
breaks = breaks_extended()(limits)

palette(rescale(x))
```

```{python}
label_comma()(breaks)
```

On a linear scale, the four smallest values map to nearly the same colour.
Rescaling after a log transform spreads these values more evenly across
the palette. The transform also supplies suitable breaks and labels.

```{python}
from mizani.transforms import log10_trans

trans = log10_trans()
breaks = trans.breaks(limits)

palette(rescale(trans.transform(x)))
```

```{python}
trans.format(breaks)
```

[](`~mizani.scale.scale_continuous`) and
[](`~mizani.scale.scale_discrete`) show how to combine these operations to
map continuous and discrete data.

## Reference

Browse the [API reference](reference/index.qmd) for each scale component.

| Section | Contents |
|---------|----------|
| [Bounds](reference/index.qmd#bounds) | Rescale, censor, squish and expand ranges of values |
| [Breaks](reference/index.qmd#breaks) | Choose the values to mark on a guide |
| [Labels](reference/index.qmd#labels) | Format break values as text |
| [Palettes](reference/index.qmd#palettes) | Map rescaled values to colours, sizes and other aesthetics |
| [Transforms](reference/index.qmd#transforms) | Transform data, for example with a logarithm, and supply matching breaks and labels |
| [Scale](reference/index.qmd#scale) | Combine scale components to map continuous and discrete data |

## Installation

Install the official release from PyPI.

```console
$ pip install mizani
```

Install the development version from GitHub.

```console
$ pip install git+https://github.com/has2k1/mizani.git@main
```

Clone the repository and install Mizani in editable mode to work on its
source code.

```console
$ git clone https://github.com/has2k1/mizani.git
$ cd mizani
$ pip install -e .
```
